items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: I played with Marshall back then. You know? And Ronnie Boykins, John Gilmore.

ctx.x: Marshall Allen. Yeah. I played with Marshall back then. You know? And Ronnie Boykins, John Gilmore. So yeah it was definitely fun and definitely I found Sun Ra very interesting. He used to read sci-fi comic books and he definitely believed he was from Saturn. So I think some of that was ahead of his time in a way, some of the pieces he wrote. The interplanetary music. And so yeah, he still sustains today. I’m glad that I was part of some of that.
There’s probably albums with — actually we have a Sun Ra collection here at Hamilton and he seemed to record constantly.

items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I started working with Sun Ra and his Arkestra... At the time the band was John Gilmore, bass player Ronnie Boykins, Marshall Allen...

ctx.x: While you were still in high school?

Yeah, I was in high school. I played with saxophone players, backed up singers, played solo piano, sang standards. Now, the drums… I got real serious about the drums after my grandmother passed away. She left some money. So what I did was I bought a car, I bought a set of drums and Wurlitzer had come out with a portable electric piano that you could take around and also had a little battery pack and a little self- contained speaker in it. I bought one of those because it enabled me to hustle gigs. I'd go to…

bands. In that period I got the opportunity… I guess, I'll go back a little bit when I guess I'd left home for a while and I was living on my own and I started working with Sun Ra and his Arkestra at a place called the Wonder Inn. Sun Ra used to rehearse there all the time. At the time the band was John Gilmore, bass player Ronnie Boykins, Marshall Allen, who is still alive. I think he's leading the Arkestra--and who else was in that band? Drummers would come and go, horn players would come and go, but I really…
